name: Field Doctor-Style Fish Pie (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
600 g Potato
330 g Hake (FISH)
3 1/2 medium Carrots
260 g Spinach
2 medium Sweet Potatoes
195 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
195 g Salmon (FISH)
110 g Fennel
1/2 Green Peppers
46 g Peas
5 tbsp Tapioca Starch
32 g Chives
5 tbsp Parsley Flat
6 tbsp Mixed Herbs
1 1/2 tbsp Lemon Zest
1 1/2 tsp White Miso [SOYA beans, cultured rice, sea salt, water]
1/8 Lemon Juice
1 tsp Sea Salt
1 1/2 tsp Flax Seeds
1 1/4 tsp Black Pepper
3/4 tsp Nutmeg Ground
directions:
1. Mash: Boil potato and sweet potato until soft; mash with extra virgin olive oil, chives, nutmeg, salt and pepper.

2. Filling veg: Soften carrot, fennel and green pepper with chives in extra virgin olive oil. Add peas.

3. Fish sauce: Stir in soy milk, white miso, lemon juice, lemon zest, herb mix and parsley. Gently poach chunks of hake and salmon in the sauce until just opaque — do not boil hard. Thicken with tapioca slurry. Fold in spinach and flax seeds. Season with black pepper and sea salt.

4. Assemble & bake: Filling in dish(es), mash on top. Bake 190°C fan 25–35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Fish Pie (Low FODMAP) (~383 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/fish-pie-low-fodmap
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~383 g x 8 = 3064 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~329 g (inferred ~10.73% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~46 g (inferred ~1.50% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
